runtime_boundary: Represents the language-model package rather than the underlying MLX array framework, and covers Apple silicon execution only.
model_management: Models are fetched from the Hugging Face Hub by identifier, and the package can quantize models and upload the result back to the Hub. Prompt caches persist to disk for reuse across generations.
hardware_requirements: Execution targets Apple silicon through MLX. No other accelerator or operating system is supported.
operational_controls: Generation and sampling parameters are set per command or per call. Distributed execution is available through the MLX distributed interface.
strengths: First-party Apple silicon execution path with quantization, upload, and low-rank or full fine-tuning in one package.
Hugging Face Hub integration reaches a large published catalogue of MLX-compatible models with a single command.
Usable as a Python module, a set of command-line tools, and a local server without additional components.
tradeoffs: Apple silicon is the only supported target, so the package cannot serve mixed or non-Apple fleets.
The bundled server is explicitly documented as not recommended for production because it implements only basic security checks.
Serving capability is minimal, with no documented continuous batching, metrics, or administrative surface.
license_note: The repository publishes a single MIT license file covering the package.

license_evidence.scope: Repository-wide license file for the MLX LM package
